citations.claim: total energy at first violating step far exceeds budget, with zero controller work
energy one step before was normal, proving jump occurs on step 28 during body-body contact
heavy body gained huge spurious x-velocity (was 0 before) during collision

counterfactual.change: set both bodies restitution e to 0.0 (was 0.9 and 0.7); with inelastic impact the collision dissipates energy instead of creating it, so energy_bound passes

explanation: No controller work (controller disabled, work=0) so energy should be <= E0 plus tolerance. Steps 25-27 show steady energy ~2297 J with body 1 moving vertically (vx=0, vy~10.5) and body 0 approaching. At step 28 the two circles touch (gap 0.044) and the restitution impulse produces unphysical energy: body 1 jumps from speed ~10.46 to 39.56 with vx=-36.30, body 0 speed ~35.10, total energy 11025 J (~4.8x). Likely cause is restitution impulse / positional-correction adding energy for unequal masses (1 vs 12.08) with high e (0.9/0.7) at oblique fast impact, violating energy conservation beyond the 10%+5J allowance.
vision_note: Two blue circles above a dark platform move closer together from step 25 to 27 and are in contact at step 28. No large bounce or separation is yet visible in these frames, consistent with the energy jump occurring exactly at the moment of contact.
